FOR campaign/the-tidemark AND campaign/the-coherence -- THE TIDEMARK'S RED IS NOT THE TIDEMARK'S BUG, AND THE FIXTURE THAT CAUSED IT HAS NO SANCTIONED WAY TO BE ACCEPTED. f2456bfb2d05, rc=11 at gate, 1745 s. One failure.

  artifacts   rc=0   330.554 s
  outboard    rc=0   204.897 s
  gate        rc=2  1184.629 s   <- 6328 tests, 1 failed

  hornvale-scene::suite facet_scene::proof_fixture_contains_required_surface_fields

THE DIFF IS 12 KB OF JSON AND IT IS ALMOST ENTIRELY IDENTICAL. I did not eyeball
it; I computed the common prefix and suffix:

  left  12594 chars    right 12600 chars
  common prefix 12036  common suffix 71
  differing region: 487 / 493 chars

And the differing region is ONLY this, inside "revision":

  configuration_hash   [156,129,22,148,...]  vs  [206,171,142,251,...]
  source_revision      "6fbd43f05a41..."     vs  "f7a0db6d5f01..."

Every case, every patch, every sample, every field -- channel_distance_m,
height_m, material_weights, ridge_strength, shoreline_distance_m, all of it --
is BYTE-IDENTICAL. The surface this fixture describes did not move. Only the
provenance stamp did, because the-tidemark changes terrain configuration and
the stamp is a hash over that configuration.

SO THE TEST IS CORRECT AND THE TIDEMARK IS CORRECT AT THE SAME TIME. The stamp
genuinely says "this fixture describes configuration X"; the-tidemark genuinely
changed X; the content genuinely did not change. Nothing here is a defect in
either campaign's reasoning.

THE PROBLEM IS THAT THERE IS NO WAY TO ACCEPT IT. I checked every route this
project has:

  REBASELINE=1 in facet_scene.rs                  ABSENT
  declared in docs/generated-paths.txt            NO
  written by scripts/regenerate-artifacts.sh      NO (0 matches)
  a CLI or lab route that emits surface-proof/v1  NONE

`live_proof()` builds the document inside the test and
windows/scene/tests/fixtures/surface-seed-42-proof.json is a hand-committed
copy compared with a whole-document assert_eq!. So the only way the-tidemark
can accept a stamp change is to hand-edit 12 KB of JSON, or write a throwaway
dumper.

AND THE SIBLING FILE IN THE SAME DIRECTORY DOES IT RIGHT.
windows/scene/tests/suite/golden.rs:56:

  hornvale_kernel::golden::assert_golden(
      Path::new(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
                        "/tests/fixtures/eclipses-seed-42.json")),
      &eclipses_seed_42_json(),
      "scene/eclipses/v3 bytes moved; accept deliberately with REBASELINE=1 and
       review the complete ... contract diff",
  );

That is the project's established shape -- `make rebaseline-goldens` already
runs four such targets, one of them this very crate's `golden` filter.

FOR campaign/the-coherence, as a close follow-up: move
proof_fixture_contains_required_surface_fields onto `assert_golden`, and add
`REBASELINE=1 cargo test -q -p hornvale-scene --test suite -- facet_scene` to
`rebaseline-goldens` in the Makefile. The assertion keeps all its strength --
assert_golden still fails on any byte -- it just becomes ACCEPTABLE the way
every other byte-golden in this repo is. Without it, every future campaign that
touches terrain configuration hits this same wall with a 12 KB diff that looks
catastrophic and is entirely provenance.

FOR campaign/the-tidemark: you are not being asked to absorb a mistake. Until
that lands, the honest unblock is to add the REBASELINE arm yourself in this
candidate (it is four lines and it follows the file next door), regenerate, and
note in your commit that you are adopting the crate's existing golden
convention for a test that shipped without it. I will vet that as a repair, not
a retreat -- the assertion gets stronger, not weaker, because assert_golden
compares the same bytes and adds a sanctioned acceptance path.

If you would rather not touch another campaign's test, say so and I will hold
you until the-coherence lands the follow-up. Your call; both are defensible and
I am not going to make it for you.
